title: Read the level
summary: Scale the raw level of a tank, a whole number from 0 to 27648, to metres, and use it to hold the level near a set point with a proportional inlet.
scope: The grade runs the simulated tank in the simulator on this computer, with an analog level that follows the scaling rules of the plant map. It says nothing about the accuracy, noise or calibration of a real level transmitter, a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Scale an analog value to engineering units so that fractions of a unit are kept.
Read the plant map to find the raw range of each signal, and see what a wrong scale does to the process.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The tank reports its level as a whole number: 0 to 27648 is 0 to 1 m. The set point potentiometer gives 0 to 1000 for 0 to 1 m, and the drain potentiometer 0 to 1000 for 0 to 100 percent. In src/TankLevel.st, scale the level and the set point to metres; set the inlet to 800 percent for each metre by which the level is below the set point, limited to 0 to 100 percent; pass the drain potentiometer to the discharge valve in percent; show the level in metres on the display, and light green while the level is within 5 percent of the set point.
stages.checkpoint: The program scales both raw values once, at the top, and every later line uses metres.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The set point is raised to 0.5 m at {{t:200}} ms and the drain potentiometer is turned to 40 percent at {{t:40000}} ms. Predict the level between {{t:30000}} ms and {{t:38000}} ms, and after the drain opens.
stages.checkpoint: The level rises to about 0.5 m without ringing and stays in the band from 0.45 m to 0.55 m, before and after the drain opens: the inlet makes up the water the drain takes, with a small offset.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter has no logic: the inlet never opens, so the tank stays empty and never reaches its band. It declares the inputs and outputs. Scale the level and the set point to metres once, before any other line uses them. Every comparison must hold for fractions of a metre: a raw level of 13824 is 0.5 m, not 0 m. Then write FillCmd from the error, limited to 0 to 100 percent.
stages.checkpoint: FillCmd stays within 0 to 100 percent, and the other three outputs follow the level and the drain potentiometer.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs src/TankLevel.st against the tank of scene tank-level-control, raises the set point and opens the drain, and tests {{assertions}} assertions on the tank: it stays in its band in two windows and it never spills.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named tank-level-scaling and contains {{assertions}} assertions and passes them all.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the display while the inlet closes as the level nears the set point. Open the plant map and find the range of Tank1.level: it is the 27648 you divided by.
stages.checkpoint: The level display reads the same number of metres as the tank.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A proportional inlet has no memory: when the drain opens the level settles a little below the set point, because the inlet only opens in proportion to the error. The next lesson adds integral and derivative terms. A wrong scale does not give a small error: with an integer division the program reads 0 m, keeps the inlet open and the tank spills.
stages.checkpoint: State why the same mistake in the set point scale would leave the tank empty.

hints.text: Look at the types: LevelRaw and SetPointRaw are INT, and an INT divided by an INT drops the fraction. The plant map gives the raw span of each signal, and the error is the set point minus the level, in metres.

Declare LevelM : REAL and SetM : REAL in VAR, then write LevelM := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 27648.0; SetM := INT_TO_REAL(SetPointRaw) / 1000.0; FillCmd := 800.0 * (SetM - LevelM); IF FillCmd > 100.0 THEN FillCmd := 100.0; END_IF; IF FillCmd < 0.0 THEN FillCmd := 0.0; END_IF; DrainCmd := INT_TO_REAL(DrainRaw) / 10.0; LevelShown := LevelM; Green := ABS(SetM - LevelM) <= 0.05 * SetM;

faultCases: The starter has no logic: the inlet never opens, so the tank stays empty and never reaches its band.
